story_type: two boaters on a capsized hull far offshore, swimmer tows them clear, basket hoists
hook: Their boat flipped 35 miles out. They waited on the hull.
narration: Their boat had flipped thirty-five miles off the North Carolina coast.
Two people were aboard. One sat on top of the hull as the swells rolled under it.
A Coast Guard helicopter crew from Air Station Elizabeth City found them.
The rescue swimmer dropped in and pulled one of them away from the wreck.
Swimmers move people clear of a capsized boat before a hoist, because the rotor wash can push the hull and loose gear into anyone close by.
Then the basket came down, with the swells lifting them both.
[short pause] One at a time, the basket rode the cable up to the cabin door.
outcome: The Coast Guard hoisted both of them off the sinking boat and into the helicopter.

location_card.place: 35 miles off Ocean Isle Beach, N.C.

title: Flipped 35 miles off North Carolina
description:
On March 8, 2015, a Coast Guard helicopter crew from Air Station Elizabeth City hoisted two people from a sinking, capsized boat about 35 miles southeast of Ocean Isle Beach, North Carolina.
